Level 2 · Intermediate · Week 4

While Loops and Game Loops

A while loop repeats until something changes, and every game is a loop.

What you will learn

  • How a while loop keeps going until something changes.
  • How to spot and stop an infinite loop.
  • How to keep asking until the player types a good answer (input validation).
  • How a loop inside a loop turns a list of strings into pixel art.

The big idea: repeat until something changes

A for loop knows how many times it will go round. A while loop does not: it checks a condition at the top, and goes round again while the condition is True.

This prints 3, 2, 1, Go!. The line n = n - 1 is the change: without it, n stays 3, the check is always True, and the loop never ends. That is an infinite loop.

TipStuck in a loop?

Press the red Stop button in Thonny’s toolbar. Then ask two questions: What is checked? and What changes inside the loop, so the check can become False?

while True and break

Sometimes it is easier to loop “for ever” and jump out when you are done. break leaves the loop straight away. Inside a function, return leaves the loop and the function.

Keep asking until the answer is good

while True:
    answer = input("Type yes or no: ").lower()
    if answer == "yes" or answer == "no":
        break                       # good answer: leave the loop
    print("Please type yes or no.")
print("Thanks!")

Checking the player’s answer like this is called input validation. Games do it all the time, so a typo never crashes them. answer.isdigit() is True only if the answer is made of the digits 0–9: then int(answer) is safe.

A loop inside a loop: pixel art

A picture can be a list of strings: one string for each row, one letter for each pixel. The outer loop goes down the rows. The inner loop goes along one row, pixel by pixel.

for row in grid:            # outer loop: one row at a time
    for pixel in row:       # inner loop: one letter at a time
        print(pixel)

New words

while loop
A loop that goes round again and again while its condition is True.
condition
The check at the top of a while loop, like n > 0 . It is True or False.
infinite loop
A loop that never stops, because nothing changes the condition. Press Stop!
break
Jumps out of a loop straight away.
input validation
Checking the player’s answer and asking again if it is not OK.
nested loop
A loop inside another loop, like rows and pixels.
game loop
The loop at the heart of a game: get input, update, show, repeat.

Homework: While Loops and Game Loops

15–20 minutes. Do Core first; Challenge and Creative are optional.

CoreTrace it first (paper, 4 minutes)

Before you code, follow hits_needed(30, 7) by hand. Each time round the loop, 7 is taken away from health and 1 is added to hits. Keep going until health is 0 or less.

round health hits
start 30 0
1 23 1
2
3
4
5

So hits_needed(30, 7) gives back: (blank to fill in)

CoreSlime Battle (Thonny, 10 minutes)

Open exercises/week04/hw-slime-battle/starter.py.

  1. TODO 1: finish hits_needed() with a while loop: while health is more than 0, take away damage and add 1 to hits.

  2. TODO 2: make ask_yes_no() keep asking until the answer is yes or no.

  3. Run it. Type maybe first. Does it ask again? ☐

Stuck in a loop? Press the red Stop button and check that health really gets smaller inside the loop.

ChallengeCount up to a target

Write a function days_to_save(goal, per_day) that uses a while loop to count how many days of saving per_day coins it takes to reach goal coins. For example days_to_save(50, 12) is 5. Add it to the bottom of your Slime Battle file (above if __name__ == "__main__":) and try it in the Shell.

CreativePixel sprite design

Design a pixel sprite for a game: a slime, a pet, a spaceship or a potion. Color the squares and write the letter code for each row underneath (K, O, Y, B, S, G, R, P or . for empty). Next week you can type it into the Pixel Art program.
